gc012Revisions.delta: GC-012 implemented the missing representation: a binding row now carries a support SET (GameCore.Planning.CapabilitySupport, TargetBindingRow.Supports, DerivedBindingRule.Supports, ProposedCapability.Supporters) and the published storage carries one GameCore.Unity.Runtime.CapabilitySupportRow per supporter. The derivation-to-publication seam no longer refuses a multi-supporter slot, and AssemblyPlanner consumes the composed value and the support set instead of publishing the top-ranked candidate's raw value. A new card fixture (Packages/com.gamecore.gameplay.cards/Fixtures/Runtime/CardAdditiveScenario.cs) mounts two scoring providers on Seat A's single cards.set-bonus slot and observes the composed value with two support rows.
gc012Revisions.whyStatusUnchanged: Player evidence now closes the live-world support-set gap, but ContributionId stability across reconfiguration and TEST-005 permutations remain open.

gc012Revisions.delta: Strengthened, and a previous over-claim corrected. The archive that supported this row evidenced the five policies in the pure composition kernel and the protocol fixtures; it did NOT evidence an Additive slot reaching a live world with its composed value, because the seam refused any slot with more than one supporter (GC-011 recorded exactly that). GC-012 removed the refusal and added the end-to-end fixture, so the row's claim is now true of the implementation as well as of the kernel.
gc012Revisions.whyStatusUnchanged: The 613/613 EditMode suite and 5/5 W4 IL2CPP probe runs now evidence the composed +5 value and two support rows end-to-end; the five-policy pure evidence remains archived.

gc012Revisions.delta: A previous over-claim corrected and the gap closed. The archived evidence covered envelope admission, route resolution, capacity/backpressure, dedup and RequestResult; it did not cover the envelope's optional 'expected domain version if needed' clause, which was DEAD DATA (written in the constructor, read nowhere, and excluded even from the admission idempotency hash). GC-012 added GameCore.Unity.Runtime.IDomainVersionAuthority and WorldMessagePlane.BindDomainVersion: the guard is now checked at admission against the route's declared authority, a mismatch is refused as StalePlan before the owner's lane, and the guard participates in the idempotency hash. The card table's CardTableDomainVersion and the narrative dialogue's DialogueDomainVersion are the two declared authorities.
gc012Revisions.whyStatusUnchanged: The new EditMode regression passed: stale expected version rejects before enqueue, a changed guard conflicts with the same request ID, and the current version admits/commits. Both family player probes passed 5/5; no player assertion independently injects a stale envelope.

On this revision it finds zero forbidden edges over 38 assemblies and 697 kernel types. The runtime half (loaded assembly graph in the stripped player) passed in five -probeW4Profile player runs.

gc012Revisions.delta: Doc gap closed on GC-015's report: 00 P-032 requires a `Reset` to be 'manifest-supported', but 05's `StateSlotSpec` row and the `GameCore.Contracts.StateSlotSpec` manifest DTO had no reset member, and `OwnershipSchedulePipeline.OptionsOf` derived its options only from `LastSupport`, so no manifest could ever declare reset support. Fixed additively: `StateSlotSpec` gained a second constructor overload (`bool resetSupported, string? resetReason`) plus `ResetSupported` and `ResetReason` properties, the original constructor chains to it, `OptionsOf` now reads the manifest, and 05 section 3/4 name both the reset policy and the explicit `Reset` request. The proposal half (`SlotChangeKind.Reset` + `SlotPolicyRequest.Reason`) already existed and is reused, so GC-015's executors need no change.
gc012Revisions.whyStatusUnchanged: The row's status is unchanged by this correction: the change makes the existing P-032 machinery reachable from content rather than adding a new capability.
